newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar climbs to 117 yen in early Tokyo trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar climbs to 117 yen in early Tokyo trade.

text.p: The dollar began the first business day of the year in Japan in a bullish mood and climbed to 117.00 yen, a near 46-month high, in early trade on Monday, dealers said.
But after touching 117.00 yen, its highest level since March 29, 1993, the dollar quickly slipped back to trade at around 116.65 yen, they said.
It had reached a high of 116.70 yen in New York on Friday before ending at around 116.33 yen.
The early gains in Tokyo were prompted by purchases by bank traders related to commercial settlements early in the session.

Sentiment was bullish towards the dollar after strong rallies in U.S. stocks on Friday in New York and prospects of a further weakening in Tokyo stocks. A strong dollar makes dollar-based assets more attractive to investors. Dealers expect the greenback to reach 118 yen by the end of January.

Tokyo stocks slipped in early morning trade, dragged down by the weaker yen. Dealers see the key Nikkei index of 225 leading shares drifting close to the 19,000 point level during the day. It ended at 19,361.35 on December 30. Key March Japanese government bonds also fell sharply in early trade.
Concerns are rising over a "triple weakness" in Japanese financial markets in which the yen is sold as capital flows out of Japanese stocks and bonds.
